$comment: Terminology + register policy for Lisse website translations. Translators (human or AI) MUST follow this for every locale. Tokens that must appear verbatim in output are enforced by i18n/do-not-translate.json + scripts/validate-translations.ts.
register: Precise, technical, developer-facing — not marketing-flowery. Use the formal/informal 'you' that is conventional for developer documentation in the target language (e.g. de: Sie or du per project norm; ja: です/ます; pt-BR: você). Keep UI labels and button text concise.

terms.lisse: Brand and npm scope (@lisse/*). NEVER translate or transliterate. Lowercase 'lisse' is the wordmark; 'Lisse' capitalized in running prose. Keep verbatim.
terms.squircle: Coined technical term. Keep VERBATIM in Latin-script locales. For zh-Hans / ja / ko, keep the Latin word 'squircle' verbatim (a parenthetical gloss on first use is allowed); a native reviewer should confirm before merge.
terms.superellipse: Coined math term. Same policy as 'squircle' — keep verbatim.
terms.clothoid: Math term (Euler spiral). Keep verbatim, or use the established local mathematical term if one is standard.
terms.border-radius: CSS property — it is code. Keep verbatim.
terms.corner-shape: CSS property — it is code. Keep verbatim.
terms.Figma / Sketch / Apple / iOS / Chrome /: Product, company and org names. Keep verbatim.
terms.React / Vue / Svelte / SVG / CSS / npm: Framework names, acronyms, tooling. Keep verbatim.
terms.Bézier / Euler: Names in math terms. Keep verbatim.
terms.un galet lisse / cheveux lisses / une co: French phrases in the dictionary-style header definition. Keep the French verbatim (they illustrate the word's French origin).

rules: Translate the VALUE only, never the key.
Preserve every {placeholder} token exactly (same names, same count).
Never alter text inside backticks `like this`, install commands, or math formulas/symbols (e.g. |x/R|^n + |y/R|^n = 1, n = 5, 1/R, κ).
Preserve leading/trailing whitespace and sentence-joining spacing exactly as in the English value.
Numbers, units and version strings (e.g. 16 pixels, 2013, 0.6, August 2025) stay as in the source unless locale number formatting clearly applies.
